final_candidates.decision_summary: Ser→Asn in a solvent-exposed HA1 loop can create an N-glycosylation-competent context; an added glycan can modestly increase HA thermostability. Purely structural-plausibility-based, no external evidence.

Adjacent exposed-loop position with polar-conservative Ser→Asn change that could complete an N-X-S/T sequon in combination with local context. Fallback candidate ranked below S144N due to weaker sequon-plausibility.
Gln→Glu is conservative and could form a new salt bridge with nearby basic residues in the HA2 stem region, improving stability. Speculative without structural modeling, hence lowest confidence.

stop_reason.detail: Self-iteration reached diminishing returns with no evidence tools available; final Top-3 selected from the initial candidate pool.

history.rationale: Creates a potential N-linked glycosylation sequon (N-S-S) on the HA1 head; added glycans are repeatedly associated with increased HA thermostability and environmental persistence in H3N2.

Adds a nearby N-glycosylation-competent sequon context in a solvent-exposed HA1 loop; extra glycan shielding can modestly increase thermostability. No external evidence available; relies on structural plausibility only.
Glu can participate in an intra-helical i+4 ionic/hydrogen-bonding interaction in the HA2 long helix (e.g., with Lys452/Lys453), marginally stabilizing the coiled coil.
Potential new salt-bridge partner for nearby basic residues in the stem/HA2 region; speculative without structural modeling. Kept but ranked low.

Adjacent to S144 in the same exposed loop; S145N combined with 144 context could complete an N-X-S/T glycosylation site, and Ser→Asn is a conservative polar substitution. Independent of S144N as a fallback.
A polar-conservative substitution in the receptor-adjacent region that may improve local hydrogen bonding/salt-bridge network. Low confidence absent structural evidence.
